title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
description:
# Range Sum Query - Mutable

Given an integer array `nums`, handle repeated operations on the same array:

* Update one element to a new value.
* Return the sum of an inclusive index range.

Implement the `NumArray` class:

* `NumArray(int[] nums)` initializes the object with the array `nums`.
* `void update(int index, int val)` sets `nums[index]` to `val`.
* `int sumRange(int left, int right)` returns `nums[left] + nums[left + 1] + ... + nums[right]`.

Updates are assignments, not additions. Every later `sumRange` call must use the most recent value at each updated index. Every query is guaranteed to satisfy `0 <= left <= right < nums.length`.

In operation examples, the first array lists operations and the second lists their argument lists, paired by index and executed left to right. The first operation constructs the object; later operations use that same object. Outputs align by index too: constructors and void methods produce `null`; an empty argument list `[]` means no arguments.

## Example 1:

**Input:**
["NumArray", "sumRange", "update", "sumRange"]
[[[1, 3, 5]], [0, 2], [1, 2], [0, 2]]

**Output:**
[null, 9, null, 8]

**Explanation:**
`sumRange(0, 2)` returns `1 + 3 + 5 = 9`.
`update(1, 2)` changes the current array to `[1, 2, 5]`.
`sumRange(0, 2)` now returns `1 + 2 + 5 = 8`.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4`
* `-100 <= nums[i] <= 100`
* `0 <= index < nums.length`
* `-100 <= val <= 100`
* `0 <= left <= right < nums.length`
* At most `3 * 10^4` calls will be made to `update` and `sumRange`.

diagrams.caption: Point update followed by an inclusive range query

solutions.name: Fenwick Tree with Stored Values
solutions.timeComplexity: O(n log n) init, O(log n) update/query
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep a Binary Indexed Tree for prefix sums and a copy of the current array values. An update computes `delta = val - nums[index]`, stores the new value, and adds the delta to every Fenwick bucket that covers the index. A range sum is the difference of two prefix sums.

## Key Insight

The operation assigns a new value, so the tree must receive only the change from the old value to the new value. Storing the current array prevents accidentally treating `val` as an increment.

## Complexity Analysis

Building with point additions takes O(n log n) time. Each update and range query takes O(log n) time. The tree and stored values use O(n) space.

solutions.name: Recursive Segment Tree
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a segment tree where each node stores the sum of a subarray. A point update follows the path to one leaf, changes that leaf, and recomputes sums on the way back. A query recursively combines nodes that are fully inside the requested interval.

## Key Insight

The segment tree stores exactly the aggregate information needed by the mutable range-sum problem. Only O(log n) nodes change after a point update, and only O(log n) boundary paths are explored for a range query.

## Complexity Analysis

Building the tree takes O(n) time. Each update and query takes O(log n) time. The tree array uses O(n) space.

solutions.name: Iterative Segment Tree
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store leaves in the second half of an array and parent sums in the first half. Updating an index changes one leaf and then walks upward recomputing parents. A range query moves two pointers inward and collects fully covered nodes.

## Key Insight

The iterative tree has the same segment-tree idea but avoids recursion and usually has smaller constants. It also makes the inclusive range query mechanics very explicit.

## Complexity Analysis

Building the tree takes O(n) time. Each update and range query takes O(log n) time. The tree uses O(n) space.

solutions.name: Mutable Block Decomposition
solutions.timeComplexity: O(n) init, O(1) update, O(sqrt n) query
solutions.description:
## Approach

Split the array into square-root sized blocks. Store the current value of each index and the sum of each block. An update adjusts one block sum by the value delta; a query scans partial edge blocks and adds full block sums in the middle.

## Key Insight

Block decomposition is a practical middle ground between direct scanning and tree structures. It is slower than Fenwick or segment trees for long query streams, but it is simpler and still avoids scanning every cell of many long ranges.

## Complexity Analysis

Initialization takes O(n) time. Each update takes O(1) time. Each query takes O(sqrt n) time. The copied values and block sums use O(n) space.

solutions.name: Direct Scan Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store a copy of the current array. An update directly assigns `nums[index] = val`. Each range query loops from `left` to `right` and sums the current values.

## Key Insight

This baseline is simple and useful for validating update semantics. It makes the assignment behavior obvious, especially when the same index is updated multiple times.

## Complexity Analysis

Construction copies the array in O(n) time. Each update takes O(1) time, and each query takes O(n) time in the worst case. The copied array uses O(n) space.
